title: Portability of Fortran's 'do concurrent' on GPUs
problem: Standard Fortran 'do concurrent' constructs lack consistent cross-vendor GPU support, with NVIDIA implementations mature but Intel and AMD platforms lagging. Unclear when unified memory systems suffice versus when explicit directive-based APIs for data movement are required for portability and performance.
motivation: Standardized language constructs for GPU acceleration improve code portability, maintainability, and reduce vendor lock-in compared to external APIs.
method: The authors implement and compile the production HipFT solar surface flux code using Fortran 'do concurrent' across NVIDIA, Intel, and AMD GPU platforms. They evaluate performance on both data center and consumer GPUs while analyzing implementation details and trade-offs between unified memory and directive-based data movement strategies.
key_novelty: First comprehensive cross-vendor evaluation of Fortran 'do concurrent' portability on NVIDIA, Intel, and AMD GPUs using a production HPC application.
contributions: Cross-platform portability evaluation of do concurrent across three GPU vendors
Guidance on when unified memory versus directive-based APIs for data movement should be used
Performance characterization on data center and consumer GPU platforms
Compiler implementation and compilation recommendations per vendor

metrics.other: performance results on data center and consumer platforms

primary_theme: Standardized language portability across GPU vendors
